original_question: If F is finitely generated over a prime field or over an algebraically closed field and D is a division algebra over F, are there only finitely many other division algebras over F with exactly the same finite splitting fields as D?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in the Introduction: the finiteness of the equivalence class of a finite-dimensional central division algebra under the relation of having exactly the same finite splitting fields; the nearby context is Proposition 1.2 (reduction in the introduction) and Theorem 1.3 (the paper’s main positive evidence over a rational function field in the prime-torsion case). ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~chernous/ChernousovPublications/survey080114.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already gets the main mathematical content right: it asks about a field satisfying the paper’s introductory hypothesis, fixes a division algebra over that field, and asks whether only finitely many other division algebras have exactly the same finite splitting fields. That is the right conjectural finiteness problem. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~chernous/ChernousovPublications/survey080114.pdf))
missing_details: The paper works with finite-dimensional central division algebras over the base field F (equivalently, their Brauer classes), not arbitrary division algebras merely containing F in the center. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~chernous/ChernousovPublications/survey080114.pdf))

The objects are counted up to F-isomorphism / Brauer class: the natural formulation is a finite set of Brauer classes [D'] in Br(F), each represented by a central division F-algebra. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~chernous/ChernousovPublications/survey080114.pdf))

The phrase 'same finite splitting fields' should be made explicit: for every finite field extension L/F, L splits D if and only if L splits D'. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~chernous/ChernousovPublications/survey080114.pdf))

The comparison is over the same base field F throughout; D' must also be a finite-dimensional central division F-algebra. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~chernous/ChernousovPublications/survey080114.pdf))

The nearby introductory context recasts the problem in Brauer-group language and then studies a prime-torsion rational-function-field case in Theorem 1.3, so the stand-alone question should keep the conjecture itself separate from that proved special case. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~chernous/ChernousovPublications/survey080114.pdf))
refined_question: Let F be a field finitely generated over its prime subfield or over an algebraically closed field. If D is a finite-dimensional central division F-algebra, is the set of Brauer classes [D'] in Br(F), where D' ranges over finite-dimensional central division F-algebras such that for every finite field extension L/F one has D ⊗F L split if and only if D' ⊗F L split, finite? ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~chernous/ChernousovPublications/survey080114.pdf))
justification: This rewrite stays with the paper’s introductory finiteness conjecture rather than broadening to neighboring problems about maximal subfields or to the proved prime-torsion k(t) statement. The main sharpening is to replace the informal phrase 'division algebra over F' by the paper-faithful object 'finite-dimensional central division F-algebra' and to spell out explicitly what 'the same finite splitting fields' means in quantifier form over finite extensions L/F. The surrounding discussion in the literature on this paper uses Brauer-class language for exactly this notion and identifies Theorem 1.3 as a special-case advance toward that conjectural finiteness question. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~chernous/ChernousovPublications/survey080114.pdf))
